You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

Observed one demonstration and successful solution on 2026-10-21.

## Rule
The grid has a horizontal separator row colored 2. On one side is a region/object consisting of a mostly uniform background with a pattern (demo: background 9 with foreground pixels 0); the other side may be blank and contain a lone marker of color 9. Output transfers/reflections the patterned region across the separator toward the other side, retaining the separator and painting a color-8 line at the boundary/edge where the pattern originally ended. In the demo the 2-divider was row 4, pattern filled rows 8–16 (9-based indices); output moved that 9x18 region to rows 5–13 immediately under divider and painted row14 solid 8. Rows outside operation stay background 9. This is consistent with the test: divider row5, marker 9 at row4 col26; expected transformation placed line of 8s at row3 (the object's new/target-side boundary, per successful submission), while leaving lone marker and divider unchanged and remaining background 6.

## Confirmed exact solution on test
Test 11x28: all color 6, except entire row index5 (0-based) is color2 and cell (row4,col26) is 9. Successful output preserved all rows except row index3 became 28 cells of color8. This was accepted correct.

## Caution
Initial unchanged-grid submission was wrong. One demo request consumed a cost but showed move-and-mark operation. The solver's second submission (8 line at row3) was correct.
